approach: Add a typed `athena.build-measurement/1` record in athena-data and load it in the core record store. In disk.rs add `Athena::measure_build`, which takes a small `CargoBuilder` trait (only the cargo build and the sccache stats read). It creates two detached git worktrees of HEAD under the state directory, each with its own target directory. It builds each, measures T (bytes of the first target dir), S (tracked-file bytes of a worktree) and the sccache counts, commits the record, and removes the worktrees and targets on every path. In hestia.rs add a pure `measure_build_due` (no record, or the stored Cargo.lock blob id differs from HEAD's) and `Athena::measure_build_pass`. `hestia_sweep_with` reaches the pass through `hestia_sweep_measuring`, which takes the builder so a test can inject a counting fake. status.rs loads the latest record into a pre-rendered line on `StatusView`, and display.rs prints it. main.rs gets a `measure-build` subcommand that uses the real cargo builder. Docs and changelog say the numbers come from records and quote no figure. Two files outside the brief's list, store.rs and display.rs, are kept because the feature does not work without them (see decisions 7 and 8).

decisions.choice: The cargo and sccache work sits behind a `CargoBuilder` trait: `build(worktree, target_dir) -> BuildRun{seconds, sccache}` and `sccache_installed()`. Worktree creation, T and S sizing, hashing, record assembly, cleanup and record writing stay in `measure_build` and run as real code in tests.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for a fake builder, but the logic under test (sizes, record assembly, cleanup) must not live in the double. The fake only returns fixed seconds and counts, and writes a file of known length into the target dir it is handed.

rejected.option: Make the whole measurement one trait method that returns a finished record
rejected.why: The fake would then contain the logic under test.

rejected.option: Time the build inside `measure_build` with Instant
rejected.why: A fake build returns at once, so a test could not assert exact build times. The real builder times its own cargo run.

decisions.choice: The sweep trigger is `Athena::measure_build_pass`, called from `hestia_sweep_with` through `hestia_sweep_measuring(checks, ui, builder)`. It is not a `Check` run by `run_sweep`.
decisions.reason: A `Check` cannot reach the records or commit one (the hestia module docs say so for review passes). Putting the pass in `hestia_sweep_with` keeps a double cold build out of `athena drain`, which also calls `review_passes`. `hestia_sweep_measuring` skips the model-driven review passes, so the test needs no agent fake.

rejected.why: It runs at the start of every drain, which would put two cold builds in front of a drain.
`default_checks` returns `Box<dyn Check>` with a 'static bound, and `Check::run` cannot commit a record.

decisions.choice: The Cargo.lock identity is the git blob id from `git.rev_parse("<head>:Cargo.lock")`, stored as `cargo_lock_hash`. If HEAD has no Cargo.lock the pass does nothing.
decisions.reason: It needs no new dependency, changes exactly when the file content changes, and keeps the sweep from running real cargo in the many test repositories that have no Cargo.lock.

rejected.option: Hash the lock file bytes with `athena_data::sha256_hex`
rejected.why: It needs a full read and adds nothing over the blob id.
It would re-measure on every landing.

decisions.choice: sccache is recorded as `SccacheFigures::{NotInstalled, Measured{first, second}}`, each side holding hits and misses. The real builder sets RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache and CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, runs `sccache --zero-stats` before each build, and parses the text of `sccache --show-stats` with a unit-tested `parse_sccache_stats`. If sccache is installed but the text cannot be parsed, the measurement errors and writes no record.
decisions.reason: The question behind D84 is whether the second worktree hits what the first missed, so per-build counts are needed. 'Not installed' must be distinguishable from zero hits, and a parse failure must not be recorded as zero.

rejected.why: The schema was not seen in the repo; the text lines are simpler to test.

decisions.choice: The status line is built in status.rs by `build_measurement_line` and carried in `StatusView.build_measurement`. display.rs prints it verbatim. The same line is reused for the `measure-build` summary.
decisions.reason: The acceptance test lives in status.rs. The JSON status output also carries the field.

rejected.why: The status.rs test could not see it.

decisions.choice: The record path is `records/build-measurements/<month>/<id>.json`, with `deny_unknown_fields` and a `validate` (finite non-negative seconds, non-empty lock hash and commit). `Records` gains `build_measurements`, sorted by (at, id), and `has_record_id` covers it.
decisions.reason: This follows the code-health baseline and throughput review pattern. The existing `check_record_file` path check enforces the location. The sweep's 'no record exists' test needs the record in the records.

rejected.option: Store it in the state directory
rejected.why: The request asks for a typed measurement record that round-trips through the records schema.

decisions.choice: Keep crates/athena-core/src/store.rs in the change (finding 2). It adds a `Records.build_measurements` field, a load arm, the sort and `has_record_id`, about 8 lines, and nothing else.
decisions.reason: This is a necessity, not scope creep. `Records::load` has a catch-all `other` arm that calls `job_of(..).expect("every other record names its job")`. The moment a build-measurement file is on the tree, loading panics unless an explicit arm exists. Status and the sweep both load records, so they would crash. The brief's own file list has no other place where the loader lives.

rejected.option: Have status.rs and hestia.rs scan the tree for the record themselves
rejected.why: The generic loader would still panic on the new kind, and two private readers would duplicate `RecordSet`.

rejected.option: Leave store.rs out and let the loader panic
rejected.why: A repository holding a measurement record would crash `athena status` and the sweep.

decisions.choice: Keep crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs in the change (finding 3). It adds one `writeln!` of `v.build_measurement` in `status()` and one rendering test.
decisions.reason: Every text line of `athena status` is rendered by `display::status`; main.rs only prints its result (main.rs line 1210). The request says `athena status` shows the latest values, so the line must be printed there. The JSON path already carries the field because `StatusView` is serialized.

rejected.option: Print the line from main.rs after `display::status`
rejected.why: It would land after the `next` lines, outside the status layout, and split rendering across two files.

rejected.option: Put the text into an existing printed field such as `next`
rejected.why: It mislabels data and breaks consumers of that field.

Required, not in the brief's list: add `Records.build_measurements`, a load arm before the `other` arm that would panic on a record with no job, the sort and `has_record_id`.

Add the `CargoBuilder` trait, `BuildRun`, the real `CargoBuild`, `parse_sccache_stats`, `dir_bytes` and `source_bytes` helpers, `Athena::measure_build`, and the fake-builder tests. Update the module docs.

Add `measure_build_due`, `Athena::measure_build_pass` (Cargo.lock and free-disk guards) and `hestia_sweep_measuring`; `hestia_sweep_with` calls review passes, then `hestia_sweep_measuring` with `CargoBuild`. Update the module docs and add the sweep tests.
Required, not in the brief's list: print `v.build_measurement` in `display::status`, with a rendering test.
Add the `MeasureBuild { json }` subcommand with help text, its dispatch arm calling `Athena::measure_build` with `CargoBuild`, and a parse test.
Extend the `disk` and `hestia` entries in the module docs. No new module.
Keep D145 marked accepted (decided by the brain under Sri's delegation, 2026-10-29) and rewrite the A1 measurements entry to point at `athena measure-build` records, with no figures.
Section 12, job 1: a short note that A1 is the `athena measure-build` command and its record. The accepted status line stays.
Add an Unreleased entry for the command, the sweep trigger and the status line; reword the earlier A1 bullet. No measured figure.

steps: Read crates/athena-data/src/records.rs around `CodeHealthBaseline` and `ThroughputReview`. Grep `AnyRecord::ThroughputReview` across the workspace for every exhaustive match to extend.

In records.rs add `BUILD_MEASUREMENT_SCHEMA = "athena.build-measurement/1"`, `SccacheCounts{hits,misses}`, `SccacheFigures::{NotInstalled, Measured{first,second}}` and `BuildMeasurement{id, at, commit, cargo_lock_hash, target_bytes, source_bytes, first_build_seconds, second_build_seconds, sccache}` with `deny_unknown_fields`, `latest()` and `validate()`. Add the `AnyRecord::BuildMeasurement(Box<..>)` variant with its serde rename, a `parse` validation arm, `canonical_path` (`records/build-measurements/<month>/<id>.json`) and a `schema` arm. Add the round-trip and validation tests (criterion 2).
In store.rs add `build_measurements` to `Records`, the load arm before `other`, the sort by (at, id) and the `has_record_id` clause. Fix any other exhaustive matches the grep found.

In disk.rs define `pub struct BuildRun{seconds: f64, sccache: Option<SccacheCounts>}` and `pub trait CargoBuilder { fn sccache_installed(&self)->bool; fn build(&self, worktree:&Path, target_dir:&Path)->Result<BuildRun>; }`. Add the real `CargoBuild`: it runs `cargo build --locked --workspace --all-targets` in the worktree with CARGO_TARGET_DIR set and times it with Instant. When sccache is installed it sets RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache and CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, zeroes the stats before the build and reads `--show-stats` after. Add the pure `parse_sccache_stats(&str)->Option<SccacheCounts>`.

In disk.rs add `dir_bytes(&Path)->u64` (recursive sum of file lengths), `source_bytes` (sum of tracked file sizes via `git.ls_files()` and metadata) and `Athena::measure_build(&self, &dyn CargoBuilder, &dyn Ui)->Result<BuildMeasurement>`. It takes HEAD and the Cargo.lock blob id by `rev_parse("<head>:Cargo.lock")` (an error if absent), creates `state.root()/measure-build/{a,b}` and `target-{a,b}`, runs `git worktree add --detach` for each, builds A then B, and sets T from `dir_bytes(target-a)` and S from worktree A. It removes the worktrees (`worktree remove --force`) and targets on every path, builds the record with a fresh `RecordId`, and commits it with `commit_records` and an `Athena-Record` trailer.
In disk.rs add the fake-builder tests (installed with counts; not installed; builder error still cleans up) and the `parse_sccache_stats` tests (criterion 1).

In hestia.rs add `pub fn measure_build_due(latest: Option<&BuildMeasurement>, lock_hash: &str)->bool` and `Athena::measure_build_pass(&self, builder, ui)->Result<Option<BuildMeasurement>>`. The pass does nothing if HEAD has no Cargo.lock, and nothing (with a line saying so) if free disk is below `jc.config.min_free_gb()`. Otherwise it loads the records and calls `measure_build` only if due.

In hestia.rs add `hestia_sweep_measuring(&self, checks, ui, builder)`: the measure pass (its result goes to `ui` as a `hestia     build measurement: ...` line, an error as 'could not run'), then `hestia_sweep(checks)`. `hestia_sweep_with` runs `review_passes` and then `hestia_sweep_measuring` with `CargoBuild`. Update the module docs. Add the sweep test with the counting fake (criterion 3).

In status.rs add `pub fn build_measurement_line(Option<&BuildMeasurement>)->String` (T and S through `format_bytes`, both times, the cache figures or 'sccache not installed', or the 'none yet' line). Add `StatusView.build_measurement: String`, filled from `BuildMeasurement::latest(&records.build_measurements)` in `status()`. Add the tests (criterion 4).

In display.rs print `v.build_measurement` in `status()`, with a rendering test. In main.rs add `MeasureBuild { json: bool }` with a help comment explaining the two cold worktree builds and the record, its dispatch arm, and a parse test (criterion 5).

Update the `disk` and `hestia` lines of the lib.rs module docs. Rewrite the A1 entry in docs/decisions.md and keep D145's accepted heading. Add the note in async-drain.md section 12. Add the CHANGELOG entry and reword the A1 bullet. State no measured figure anywhere.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Confirm with `git status` that athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github/ and the drain tests are unchanged.

risks.risk: Two real cold builds fill the disk or run for a long time inside a sweep.
risks.mitigation: The sweep pass does nothing when HEAD has no Cargo.lock, so test repositories never run cargo. It refuses when `df_free_bytes` is below `jc.config.min_free_gb()` and says so in a line. Worktrees and target dirs are removed on success and on error.
The measurement runs in `hestia_sweep_with` only, which `athena hestia sweep` calls. `review_passes`, which the drain calls, is left unchanged, and no drain test is edited.

risks.risk: The measurement re-runs forever or never.
risks.mitigation: A test shows the pass is a no-op when the stored hash equals HEAD's, and runs again after the blob id changes.

risks.risk: A new AnyRecord variant breaks an exhaustive match elsewhere, or panics in the loader's catch-all arm.
risks.mitigation: Add the variant to every exhaustive match on AnyRecord. The producer greps `AnyRecord::ThroughputReview` across the workspace (earlier count: records.rs, store.rs, hestia.rs only) to find each site, and adds the store.rs arm so the `other` arm never sees the new kind. The sweep and status tests plus the full suite catch a miss.

risks.risk: The docs or changelog claim a measured figure.
risks.mitigation: CHANGELOG and docs say only that the numbers come from records. Fixture figures live only in test modules. The policy tests in the suite scan the docs.

risks.risk: The sccache server is shared, so stats could mix the two builds.
risks.mitigation: The real builder runs `sccache --zero-stats` before each build and reads the stats right after. If sccache is installed but its stats cannot be parsed, the measurement errors rather than recording a zero.

risks.risk: The test suite's own runs become slow or recursive through a nested cargo build.
risks.mitigation: The new tests use only temp repos and the fake builder, which never runs cargo. Existing tests are not edited.

demonstrations.method: Test in disk.rs. Entry point: `Athena::measure_build(&dyn CargoBuilder, &dyn Ui)` on an Athena over a temp git repo with a committed Cargo.lock and two tracked files of known sizes, built with the existing `crate::code_health::tests::set_up` pattern. Guard and precondition: HEAD has a Cargo.lock. Seam: a `FakeBuilder` in the test module, passed as `&dyn CargoBuilder`; the trait is added in step 4 and does not exist today. The fake writes a file of known length into the target_dir it is given and returns fixed seconds (such as 61.5 and 12.25) and sccache counts. Worktree creation, sizing, hashing and record writing are the real production code. Two tests: sccache installed, and `sccache_installed() == false`. `parse_sccache_stats` has unit tests for real-looking text and garbage.
demonstrations.observes: After `Records::load`, `build_measurements` holds one record with `target_bytes` equal to the written file length, `source_bytes` equal to the sum of the tracked file sizes, `first_build_seconds` 61.5, `second_build_seconds` 12.25, and `sccache` equal to Measured{first, second} (or NotInstalled). The fake saw two distinct worktree paths and two distinct target dirs. After the call neither worktree nor target dir exists, also after a fake that returns an error.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the behavior no record is committed, or T, S, the build times or the cache figures differ from the fixture, and an assertion fails. In the not-installed case, a record that claims counts fails the `NotInstalled` assertion. If the logic were missing and only the fake returned a record, the sizes asserted from real files would not match.

demonstrations.method: Test in records.rs beside `a_throughput_review_has_a_path_a_schema_and_round_trips`. Entry points: `AnyRecord::to_json`, `canonical_path`, `schema` and `check_record_file(path, bytes)`. No seam: a constructed `BuildMeasurement` value, in both the `Measured` and `NotInstalled` variants. A second test calls `validate`/`check_record_file` with a NaN or negative time and an empty lock hash.
demonstrations.observes: `check_record_file(&record.canonical_path(), json.as_bytes())` returns `Ok(Some(parsed))` and `parsed == record`. The schema is `athena.build-measurement/1`. The path matches `records/build-measurements/<yyyy-mm>/<id>.json`. Bad numbers are refused with `RecordError::Invalid`, and a record at the wrong path with `Misplaced`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the `AnyRecord` variant is missing, `check_record_file` returns a parse or unknown-file error and the round trip fails. If the canonical path is wrong it returns `Misplaced`. If `validate` is missing, the bad-number case is accepted and its assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Test in hestia.rs. Entry point: `Athena::hestia_sweep_measuring(&[], &Quiet, &CountingBuilder)`, the function `hestia_sweep_with` calls after its review passes. `run_sweep` itself is a pure function over `Check`s with no records access, so the trigger is tested at this sweep entry. The split is added in step 8; it does not exist today. Guards and preconditions: HEAD has a Cargo.lock, and free disk is above `jc.config.min_free_gb()` (a real temp dir). Seam: a `CountingBuilder` with a `Cell<u32>` call counter, defined in the test and injected as `&dyn CargoBuilder`; it writes a small file into its target dir and returns fixed seconds. Steps: sweep once with no record; sweep again; commit a changed Cargo.lock; sweep a third time. `measure_build_due` also has pure unit tests. A repo with no Cargo.lock at HEAD is swept and gets zero calls.
demonstrations.observes: After sweep 1 the builder was called twice (two builds), one record exists, and the output has a `build measurement` line. After sweep 2 the count is unchanged and there is still one record. After the Cargo.lock change, sweep 3 raises the count by two, there are two records, and the newer one has the new `cargo_lock_hash`.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the sweep never runs the measurement, the builder call count stays 0 after sweep 1. If it ignores the stored hash, the count is 2 after sweep 2, or stays at 2 after the lock change. Each fails an assertion. If store.rs had no load arm, `Records::load` would panic in this test.

demonstrations.method: Test in status.rs. Entry points: `Athena::status()` on a temp repo, and the pure `build_measurement_line(Option<&BuildMeasurement>)`. The test commits two records through `commit_records` (the newer must win) and reads `StatusView.build_measurement`. A second case has no record. A display.rs test (step 10) renders `display::status(&view)` and checks that the line is in the printed text. No fake is needed; `StatusView.build_measurement` and `build_measurement_line` are added in step 9.
demonstrations.observes: The line contains the newest record's T and S (through `format_bytes`), both build times, and the hit and miss counts, or the words 'sccache not installed'. It names the short commit and the time. With no record it reads a clear line, such as 'build measure: none yet (athena measure-build, or the Hestia sweep, makes one)'.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `StatusView` carries no measurement line, the test finds no `build measure` line. If the status shows an older record, the values differ from the newest record's and the assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Grep `MeasureBuild` and `measure-build` in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs; run the parse test in main.rs using `Cli::try_parse_from(["athena","measure-build"])`, like the existing `hestia_review_takes_backfill...` test; and run the help. The match arm calls `open(true)?.measure_build(&CargoBuild, &Terminal)`, with `CargoBuild` the real builder from disk.rs. The subcommand and its arm are added in step 10. open_questions: Criterion 3 says 'run_sweep runs the measurement'. `run_sweep` is a pure function over `Check`s with no records access, so the plan tests the sweep entry `hestia_sweep_measuring`, which `hestia_sweep_with` calls. Confirm that reading.
Which cargo invocation is the 'workspace cold build'? The plan assumes `cargo build --locked --workspace --all-targets`, so T covers test targets. Say if it should match the check builds exactly.

A measurement that fails (cargo error, unreadable sccache stats) writes no record, so each later sweep tries again with two cold builds. The plan adds no failure marker, to stay small. Add one if wanted.
`git worktree add` writes `.git/worktrees` metadata in the real repository while the run lasts. The plan removes it afterwards, even on error. Confirm Athena's environment may do this.
The code did not show whether the installed `sccache --show-stats` labels are 'Cache hits' and 'Cache misses'. The parser accepts lines starting with those words and fails loudly otherwise.
